title: Fixed-width helper chaining and Float64 Wasm bridge
objective: Fix generic fixed-width transitive native helper chaining, then implement a production WebAssembly bridge for same-source Float64Buffer kernels with bounded marshalling, float64 results, mutation-aware copyback, inspectable zero-callback core, and standalone/browser-loader differential coverage

oracles: independent fixed-width transitive helper witness with inspected word core
same-source CPython, dynamic JavaScript, native host, and WebAssembly differential
inspectable emitted C and manifest ABI

handoff.summary: The native compiler keeps proved uint64 helper chains in the word core and the production Wasm bridge now supports source-transparent Float64 scalars, Float64Buffer parameters, Float64 results, bounded wasm32 marshalling, and mutation-aware copyback. Independent witnesses cover inspectable zero-callback C, CPython/dynamic/native agreement, direct standalone WASI execution, and the browser-safe pack loader.
risks: Cross-platform production-pack integration remains for the integration lane; this lane validated Linux x64 with an actual WASI clang/sysroot.
pnpm test:baselib:strict is blocked at the unchanged base by Ruff formatting in bench/hyperelliptic/competitive/sagemath-resident.py, outside this lane's claim.
next_steps: Cherry-pick the Float64 bridge commit with the analytic period source and register _period_edge_batch_float64 in the shared production-kernel manifest.
Run the integrated analytic/browser differential and production-pack builds on Linux arm64, Windows x64, and macOS arm64.
